## What it is

Every decision the System and Information Integrity family asks your organization to make before its policy and procedures can be final: the family's key questions, then each organization-defined parameter of every SI control in the baseline, with a typical value where the [System and Information Integrity Policy](/templates/policies/si/) gives one. Download the spreadsheet, fill the "Your value" column with the people who decide, and carry the values into the policy's highlighted fields.

Typical values are starting points, not recommendations for every system. "Who decides" defaults to the role accountable for the family policy; many organizations delegate system-level values to the system owner.

## Decisions (Moderate baseline)

62 decisions.

| Decision | Control | Typical value | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who installs updates for each kind of component, and how are urgent updates approved? | SI-2, SI-2(2) | The IT operations team patches operating systems and common software monthly as standard changes; application teams update their own code and libraries; updates for known exploited vulnerabilities go through the emergency change process. | Chief Information Security Officer, with the change control board |
| Where do monitoring data and alerts go, and who triages them, at what hours? | SI-4, SI-4(2), SI-4(5) | A central security information and event management (SIEM) platform, triaged around the clock by the security operations team or a managed security service. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which malicious code, spam and monitoring protections are common controls, and which does each system own? | SI-3, SI-4, SI-8 | Endpoint detection and response, the email gateway and the SIEM platform are common controls; each system owner makes sure every component runs the agent and sends its logs, and owns application-specific detections. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Is encrypted traffic decrypted for inspection, and which categories are exempt? | SI-4(10) | Decrypted at the internet boundary proxy, with health, financial and similar personal categories exempt, as approved by legal counsel and the senior privacy official. | Chief Information Security Officer, with legal counsel and the senior privacy official |
| Where are retention periods set for each type of information, and who confirms information is disposed of at the end? | SI-12, SI-12(3) | In the organization's records retention schedule, owned by records management; each system security plan and privacy impact assessment names the periods that apply, and the system owner confirms disposal each year. | System owner, with records management |
